claims.statement: RubyGems publication and Bundler consumption cover FPT/GHEC/GHES; GHES administrators may disable the package type and release-stage reusable is comment-only. Managed users may publish to organizations, not personal namespaces.

GHEC github.com uses rubygems.pkg.github.com; another enterprise domain requires rubygems.SUBDOMAIN.ghe.com. The article's cloud examples require this override rather than establishing a universal github.com endpoint.

Prerequisites are RubyGems >=2.4.1 and Bundler >=1.6.4 in the pinned guide. Version commands and Bundler 1.13.7 sample output are unexecuted historical examples, not current installed-version observations or recommendations.

Classic PAT task-scopes apply to registry authentication; general reusable preserves GITHUB_TOKEN associated-repository publication and read-granted install exceptions. Public RubyGems operations require authentication here, unlike anonymous public Container Registry pulls.

packages-rubygems-v2 applies FPT/GHEC only: it enables granular personal/organization scope, recommends workflow GITHUB_TOKEN over PAT and supports separate Actions/Codespaces grants. Do not infer GHES v2 capability from an inactive GHES branch nested in that feature.

The v2 reusable describes REST deletion/restoration with package-admin GITHUB_TOKEN in public preview and automatic admin for publishing/explicitly connected repositories. This wording must remain qualified against post-publication linking retaining existing permissions in the access guide; linkage alone is not a verified admin grant.

Publishing tutorial stores a github Bearer credential in ~/.gem/credentials; installation sources embed USERNAME:TOKEN in URLs and bundle config credentials. These examples risk secret persistence/history/output exposure and are not permission to run them, commit credential files or expose tokens.

GHES isolation changes RubyGems registry URL: rubygems.HOSTNAME when enabled, HOSTNAME/_registry/rubygems otherwise, both wrapped with https:// in examples. NAMESPACE is v2 package owner on cloud versus repository owner in non-v2 scope.

Optional gem sources --add configures a global registry source; Bundler config associates credentials with a namespace source. Global client-state changes are separate from a project-specific dependency declaration and require intentional reviewed configuration.

Cloud v2 publication defaults private and permits granular package permissions; non-v2 default targets existing repository with gem name. Linked access inheritance is conditional on feature and org default, not visibility inheritance or universally guaranteed effective access.

Build uses gem build GEM_NAME.gemspec; push uses --key github, namespace host and illustrative GEM_NAME-0.0.1.gem. Maximum uncompressed metadata.gz must be less than 2 MB per variable; exceeding the limit fails, and the exact-equality boundary is not independently verified.

Cloud v2 github_repo metadata associates a repository at publication and allows multiple gems per repository; non-v2 metadata overrides default name-based matching. Source SSH URL metadata is not a tested connection/access or immutable artifact identity receipt.

Installation uses a gemrc source or Bundler Gemfile source block scoped to chosen gems alongside rubygems.org/rails. Versions below Bundler 1.7.0 require the documented global source alternative; source precedence and dependency provenance remain untested.

The final gem install example pins illustrative version 0.1.1, while the earlier push example is 0.0.1. These are separate examples, not a demonstrated publish/install roundtrip; Gemfile examples omit explicit versions and do not certify immutable resolution.

Linked RubyGems creation, Bundler, workflow-security and package-deletion guides remain separately scoped. No upstream client commands, credential changes, dependency downloads, package publication, accepted policy, rights clearance or native enforcement occurred.
